bug_semantics: Magento 2.4.8 storefront GraphQL allCustomerGroups (and related customerGroup / Customer.group fields) return customer-group names without enforcing Magento_Customer::group. The same GroupRepositoryInterface::getList/getById methods are ACL-gated on REST /V1/customerGroups/search, but AllCustomerGroups::resolve() only checks config customer/account_information/graphql_share_all_customer_groups, which defaults to 1. Unauthenticated GraphQL therefore enumerates group codes (Wholesale, VIP, custom B2B names). CWE-863; CVSS 2.7 PR:H C:L as scored by Adobe (public exploit is unauthenticated). Reporter Damien Retzinger. Affected in public git as 2.4.8 GA; removed in 2.4.8-p1 / LYNX-838.
flaw_origin: LYNX-732 (1b8236afe67fa961d4517e326ca278cb3daf406c, 2025-02-25) first added AllCustomerGroups.php, GetCustomerGroup.php, CustomerGroup.php, GetCustomerGroupName.php, and default-true graphql_share_* flags in Customer/etc/config.xml. The resolver calls GroupRepositoryInterface::getList() with no GraphQL user-type or Magento_Customer::group check. Immediate parent f112c7a7bba2808d4046f22eacc76791634623db has no those resolvers and no allCustomerGroups schema field.

reasoning: Vulnerability-first: CVE-2025-49549 is a published Adobe CWE-863 (not withdrawn/rejected). First-party APSB25-50 plus the credited reporter's gist and Adobe LYNX-839 KB identify the mechanism as 2.4.8 GraphQL personalization APIs leaking customer-group names. REST already requires Magento_Customer::group for GroupRepositoryInterface::getList; LYNX-732 exposed that list on anonymous GraphQL behind a default-true share flag, which is incorrect authorization / ACL bypass with C:L (names only). Adobe's PR:H/admin wording and the GHSA 'Authenticated' title do not match the public unauthenticated query; the code path and reporter PoC are unauthenticated, while the protected resource is an admin ACL. Related 2.4.8-p1 GraphQL removals (allCartRules/allCatalogRules) are the same LYNX-838 family and may map to CVE-2025-43585 or CVE-2025-49550; this case is bound to Damien's allCustomerGroups write-up. BIC search used the first-party GraphQL feature add, not an AI-first invert: git log --diff-filter=A on AllCustomerGroups.php and the LYNX-732 commit are the first write; parent tree lacks the resolvers and schema field. GitHub web-flow committed a single-parent object with no reconstructable public members, so 1b8236afe67 is a valid smallest surviving BIC. It precedes 2.4.8 GA and is absent from 2.4.8-beta2/2.4.7-p5. The 2.4.8-p1 packaging commit removes the files (fix_sha); LYNX-838 is the named develop deletion (direct_fix_sha). AI decision is BIC-only: human Adobe author Deepak Soni, GitHub as committer, no AI trailers, therefore NOT_AI.
